subject.title: fix(cron): pass allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent from cron executor for both runner paths

question: Should empty assistant output be treated as successful silence for all cron jobs, or should the flag be limited to no-deliver/silent-delivery jobs or a per-job opt-in?
rationale: The patch is mechanically sound, but the behavior changes user-visible cron status and delivery semantics in a way only maintainers can accept for existing installations.

options.title: Accept all-cron silence
options.body: Confirm that any cron empty assistant reply is a successful no-op, land this executor-boundary approach, and close or supersede overlapping PRs.

options.title: Gate by delivery or job option
options.body: Require the branch to derive the flag from delivery mode or a new explicit job setting so delivered cron jobs can still fail on empty output.

options.title: Pause for another canonical branch
options.body: Keep this PR open while maintainers select a competing implementation as the canonical fix for the linked bug.

recommendation.title: Accept all-cron silence
recommendation.body: Confirm that any cron empty assistant reply is a successful no-op, land this executor-boundary approach, and close or supersede overlapping PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent delivery and runner-boundary history makes this the best available owner for the cron silent-output policy choice.
